title: A Sleep-EDF spectral transition model did not pass stronger-baseline and negative-control checks in an independent Dublin sleep dataset
abstract: A fixed relative five-band EEG model developed in three Sleep-EDF people lowered next-epoch stage-change log loss against current stage alone in 25 independently collected UCD participants (difference -0.02179; participant bootstrap 95% interval -0.04022 to -0.00476). But history augmentation gave -0.00282 (-0.00759 to 0.00146), nonwake prediction did not improve, time-shifted features performed similarly, and shuffled-target fitting performed better. Thus this external test does not validate transition-specific physiological information. It also corrects a temporal-adjacency assumption in the precursor, without changing that pilot direction. Lawful public inputs, hashes, offline container code, derived predictions, reruns and self-checks are provided.

citations.reason: Uses the precursor development subset and model approach, adds independent-dataset challenge and corrects its temporal-adjacency assumption.
